newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX gasoline gaps up, may continue lead.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX gasoline gaps up, may continue lead.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline futures may continue to lead crude and heating oil higher with today's early price jump on Access trading providing a supportive gap up to underpin recent gains, analysts said.
Gasoline gapped bullishly higher on Wednesday, widening the usually bearish expending wedge pattern on the spot month continuation chart.
But despite recent gains this wedge formation combined with the overbought signals flagged by momentum indicators continue to fuel a bearish undertone, analysts said.

"Gasoline has gapped up already today and it remains to be seen whether the saying 'gaps are made to be filled' will apply to the August contract today", Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research in his daily report.
The August contract opened 35 cents up from Tuesday's high of 66.60 cents, pushing out the gap between the upper resistance and lower supportive trend lines on the spot month continuation chart.
The upper line which stems from June 23's trough high of 56.30 cents through July 17's 62.45 cent high had been capping the market over the past three days.
The contract finished under this level on Tuesday despite spending most of the day above it.
Analysts said the next upside target is 67.60 cents of May 23 on the spot month chart with the September contract high of 67.25 cents breached in early trade when prices to a high of 67.50.

But momentum indicators are flagging overbought with slow stochastics on the point of convergence at a high levels, usually indicating a fall to come and 14-day RSIs in the 76 percent overbought zone.

September crude finally stepped above the short term down trend line in early trade on Wednesday. The trendline stemming from May 16's $22.40 high has proved a barrier over the past three trading days.
Analysts said the market will have to hold convincingly above this level for a while if it is to get any higher.
"(NYMEX crude) is above $20 again but will need quite some support to get through $20.25 and $20.40 where the market has run into active selling in the past," Nicholas said
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said, "Today we continue to buy dips to $20, taking profits and shorting the market on selling extreme".
But she added "If gasoline is looking very strong we would steer clear of the short side fearing a break higher".

Technicals for crude remained in neutral to positive mode though there is some stiff Fibonacci resistance at $20.12, then last week's $20.20 and $20.24 from the previous week provide a near double top barrier.
July 7's $20.40 blocks the path to $21.
Initial support is at $19.77 Tuesday's low while a narrow gap up between July 22s $19.39 high to July 23s $19.40 low provides a base.

On the September chart the uptrend starting from July 21's $19.25 low remains intact and slow stochastics crossed at a fairly neutral 60 percent level then headed higher indicating room for improvement.
Heating oil is seen continuing to tick higher hugging an uptrend support line from July 21s low of 51.85 cents and taking strength from the sharp gasoline price gains.
Momentum indicators here remain in neutral territory but analysts say the market could just as easily tip lower if gasoline runs out of steam.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
